messages.subject: extreme stubbornness
parts:
I think I solved my problem.

The logic of legend spacing within ggplot2 turns out to be (in my
opinion) a bit odd (this is all in ggplotGrob(), in plot-render.r).

If there is no legend generated at all (i.e. there are no aesthetics
varying within facets), but opts(position.legend) is not specified
explicitly either, then position.legend defaults to "right" and the
legend width is set to zero (the width of the legend box) plus 0.5 lines.

If there is a legend generated and opts(position.legend) is "right" or
"left" then legend width is set to the width of the legend box plus 0.5
lines (of course).

If opts(position.legend) is "none" then legend width **is ignored in
positioning boxes** so the width is effectively zero.

So there is different spacing when rendering a ggplot object that has
no legend (and no legend.position set) and when rendering a ggplot
object that has a legend, but with the legend disabled via
legend.position="none".

This means that testing for zero width of the legend in the ggplotGrob
(as the current version of align.plots() does) is not sufficient -- you
have to look at the legend position in the original ggplot object.

I have a modified version of align.plots() that does this, and could
provide a patch, but I'm a little bit confused about where to get the
latest version of ggExtra for generating an appropriate patch: R-forge,
or googlecode?

Arguably, the logic within ggplotGrob() could (should?) be tweaked to
*not* add 0.5 lines to legendwidth when is.zero(legend) is TRUE ...

(As I mentioned in a previous message, I think I also have the
beginnings of a fix for the issue raised in February about taking
vertical strips into account. Also, it would seem to be a good idea to
replace .ggplot2:::.zeroGrob with zeroGrob() [presumably this wasn't
exposed before and is now].)

cheers
Ben Bolker
